title: Product of All Others
description:
For every position i, compute the product of all elements of the list except a[i]. Try to do it without using division (the list may contain zeros).

Constraints:

  • 2 ≤ N ≤ 1000
  • -9 ≤ a[i] ≤ 9

Input

The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the N products on one line, space-separated.
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
res = [1] * n
p = 1
for i in range(n):
    res[i] = p
    p *= a[i]
p = 1
for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
    res[i] *= p
    p *= a[i]
print(' '.join(map(str, res)))

title: Three-Way Partition
description:
Given a list and a pivot value P, rearrange the list into three groups: first all elements less than P, then all elements equal to P, then all elements greater than P. Inside each group, keep the original relative order.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 1000
  • -1000 ≤ a[i], P ≤ 1000

Input

The first line contains two integers N and P. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the rearranged list on one line, space-separated.
solution:
n, p = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
print(' '.join(map(str, [x for x in a if x < p] + [x for x in a if x == p] + [x for x in a if x > p])))

title: Next Permutation
description:
Rearrange the list into the next lexicographically greater permutation of its values. If the list is already the largest permutation, print the smallest one instead (sorted ascending). The list may contain duplicate values.

Example: 1 2 3 → 1 3 2, and 3 2 1 → 1 2 3.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 1000
  • -1000 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000

Input

The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the next permutation on one line, space-separated.
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
i = n - 2
while i >= 0 and a[i] >= a[i + 1]:
    i -= 1
if i >= 0:
    j = n - 1
    while a[j] <= a[i]:
        j -= 1
    a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
a[i + 1:] = reversed(a[i + 1:])
print(' '.join(map(str, a)))

title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
description:
You are given N closed intervals [s, e] in any order. Merge all intervals that overlap or touch (e.g. [1, 3] and [3, 5] become [1, 5]).

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 1000
  • -106 ≤ s ≤ e ≤ 106

Input

The first line contains N. Each of the next N lines contains two integers s e (s ≤ e).

Output

Print the merged intervals sorted by start, one per line, as s e.

title: Insert an Interval
description:
You are given a list of non-overlapping closed intervals sorted by start, and one new interval. Insert the new interval, merging any intervals that overlap or touch it.

Constraints:

  • 0 ≤ N ≤ 1000
  • -106 ≤ s ≤ e ≤ 106

Input

The first line contains N. Each of the next N lines contains s e. The last line contains the new interval s e.

Output

Print the resulting intervals in order, one per line, as s e.

title: Container With Most Water
description:
There are N vertical lines; line i (0-based) has height h[i]. Choose two lines that, together with the x-axis, form a container. The water it holds is min(h[i], h[j]) × (j - i). Find the maximum amount of water.

Constraints:

  • 2 ≤ N ≤ 3000
  • 0 ≤ h[i] ≤ 104

Input

The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the maximum area.

title: Shortest Window Reaching Target
description:
Given a list of positive integers and a target S, find the length of the shortest contiguous sub-list whose sum is at least S.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 3000
  • 1 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000
  • 1 ≤ S ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains two integers N and S. The second line contains N positive integers.

Output

Print the minimum length, or 0 if no such sub-list exists.
solution:
n, s = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
best = n + 1
lo = total = 0
for hi in range(n):
    total += a[hi]
    while total >= s:
        best = min(best, hi - lo + 1)
        total -= a[lo]
        lo += 1
print(best if best <= n else 0)

title: Longest Mountain
description:
A mountain is a contiguous sub-list of length at least 3 that strictly increases up to a peak and then strictly decreases (both parts must be non-empty). Find the length of the longest mountain.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 3000
  • 0 ≤ a[i] ≤ 104

Input

The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the length of the longest mountain, or 0 if there is none.

title: Three Numbers Summing to Zero
description:
Find all unique triplets of values x ≤ y ≤ z, taken from three different positions of the list, such that x + y + z = 0. Two triplets are the same if they contain the same values.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 1500
  • -105 ≤ a[i] ≤ 105

Input

The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print each triplet on its own line as x y z (ascending inside the triplet), with triplets sorted in lexicographic order. If there are none, print NONE.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description:
The list describes an elevation map where each bar has width 1. Compute how many units of rain water can be trapped between the bars after it rains.

Heights: 0 1 0 2 1 0 1 3 2 1 2 1  →  6 units

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 3000
  • 0 ≤ h[i] ≤ 104

Input

The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the total trapped water.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description:
A window of size K slides over the list from left to right, one position at a time. For every window position, report the maximum element in the window.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ K ≤ N ≤ 3000
  • -104 ≤ a[i] ≤ 104

Input

The first line contains two integers N and K. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the N - K + 1 window maximums on one line, space-separated.
solution:
from collections import deque
n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
dq = deque()
res = []
for i, x in enumerate(a):
    while dq and a[dq[-1]] <= x:
        dq.pop()
    dq.append(i)
    if dq[0] <= i - k:
        dq.popleft()
    if i >= k - 1:
        res.append(a[dq[0]])
print(' '.join(map(str, res)))

title: Subarrays Summing to K
description:
Count the number of contiguous non-empty sub-lists whose sum equals exactly K. The list may contain negative numbers and zeros.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 3000
  • -1000 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000
  • |K| ≤ 106

Input

The first line contains two integers N and K. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the count.
solution:
n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
seen = {0: 1}
s = cnt = 0
for x in a:
    s += x
    cnt += seen.get(s - k, 0)
    seen[s] = seen.get(s, 0) + 1
print(cnt)

title: Minimum Meeting Rooms
description:
Each meeting occupies the half-open time range [s, e). A room freed at time t can be reused by a meeting starting at time t. Find the minimum number of rooms needed to hold all meetings.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 2000
  • 0 ≤ s < e ≤ 106

Input

The first line contains N. Each of the next N lines contains two integers s e (s < e).

Output

Print the minimum number of rooms.
solution:
n = int(input())
ev = []
for _ in range(n):
    s, e = map(int, input().split())
    ev.append((s, 1))
    ev.append((e, -1))
ev.sort()
cur = best = 0
for _, d in ev:
    cur += d
    best = max(best, cur)
print(best)

title: Minimum Jumps to the End
description:
You start at index 0. From index i you may jump forward by any distance from 1 to a[i]. Find the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the last index.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 3000
  • 0 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000

Input

The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the minimum number of jumps, or -1 if the last index cannot be reached. If N = 1 the answer is 0.
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
jumps = end = far = 0
ans = 0
for i in range(n - 1):
    if i > far:
        break
    far = max(far, i + a[i])
    if i == end:
        jumps += 1
        end = far
        if end >= n - 1:
            break
print(jumps if far >= n - 1 or n == 1 else -1)

title: Circular Maximum Subarray
description:
The list is circular: the element after the last one is the first one. Find the maximum sum of a non-empty contiguous sub-list, where a sub-list may wrap around the end. Each element may be used at most once.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 3000
  • -104 ≤ a[i] ≤ 104

Input

The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the maximum sum.
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
total = sum(a)
bmax = cmax = bmin = cmin = a[0]
for x in a[1:]:
    cmax = max(x, cmax + x); bmax = max(bmax, cmax)
    cmin = min(x, cmin + x); bmin = min(bmin, cmin)
print(bmax if bmax < 0 else max(bmax, total - bmin))

title: First Missing Positive
description:
Find the smallest positive integer (1, 2, 3, …) that does not appear in the list. The list may contain negatives, zeros and duplicates. Bonus: solve it in O(N) time using O(1) extra space.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 3000
  • -106 ≤ a[i] ≤ 106

Input

The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the smallest missing positive integer.

title: Unique Quadruplets
description:
Count the number of unique quadruplets of values a ≤ b ≤ c ≤ d, taken from four different positions of the list, with a + b + c + d = T. Two quadruplets are the same if they consist of the same values.

An O(N4) brute force is too slow for the largest tests.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 150
  • -104 ≤ a[i] ≤ 104
  • |T| ≤ 105

Input

The first line contains two integers N and T. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the number of unique quadruplets.

title: Counting Inversions
description:
An inversion is a pair of positions i < j with a[i] > a[j] (strictly). Count the inversions in the list.

The largest tests are too big for an O(N2) double loop; think merge sort or a Fenwick tree.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 4000
  • 0 ≤ a[i] ≤ 999

Input

The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the number of inversions.
solution:
import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(10000)
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
def sort(x):
    if len(x) <= 1:
        return x, 0
    m = len(x) // 2
    l, c1 = sort(x[:m])
    r, c2 = sort(x[m:])
    res = []
    i = j = 0
    c = c1 + c2
    while i < len(l) and j < len(r):
        if l[i] <= r[j]:
            res.append(l[i]); i += 1
        else:
            res.append(r[j]); j += 1
            c += len(l) - i
    res += l[i:] + r[j:]
    return res, c
print(sort(a)[1])

title: Shortest Subarray With Sum at Least K
description:
Find the length of the shortest contiguous non-empty sub-list whose sum is at least K. Unlike the simpler version, the list may contain negative numbers, so a plain sliding window does not work.

Hint: prefix sums plus a monotonic deque give O(N).

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 3000
  • -104 ≤ a[i] ≤ 104
  • 1 ≤ K ≤ 108

Input

The first line contains two integers N and K. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the minimum length, or -1 if no such sub-list exists.
solution:
from collections import deque
n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
p = [0]
for x in a:
    p.append(p[-1] + x)
dq = deque()
best = n + 1
for j in range(n + 1):
    while dq and p[j] - p[dq[0]] >= k:
        best = min(best, j - dq.popleft())
    while dq and p[dq[-1]] >= p[j]:
        dq.pop()
    dq.append(j)
print(best if best <= n else -1)

title: Sliding Window Median
description:
A window of size K slides over the list from left to right. For each window position, report the median of the window: the middle element after sorting if K is odd, or the average of the two middle elements if K is even.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ K ≤ N ≤ 3000
  • -104 ≤ a[i] ≤ 104

Input

The first line contains two integers N and K. The second line contains N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the N - K + 1 medians on one line, separated by spaces. Print each median with exactly one decimal place (e.g. 3.0, -1.5).
solution:
from bisect import insort, bisect_left
n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
w = sorted(a[:k])
def med():
    if k % 2:
        return f"{w[k // 2]}.0"
    s = w[k // 2 - 1] + w[k // 2]
    if s % 2 == 0:
        return f"{s // 2}.0"
    return ('-' if s < 0 else '') + f"{abs(s) // 2}.5"
res = [med()]
for i in range(k, n):
    del w[bisect_left(w, a[i - k])]
    insort(w, a[i])
    res.append(med())
print(' '.join(res))
